what: A security notice as a push to an app (#13233, docs/auth/identity-and-methods.md "Notify"): the request body coax/web/api/push.c sends Apple's push service (POST /3/device/TOKEN) and Google's (POST /v1/projects/PROJECT/messages:send) for each notice coax/web/api/auth-recover.c delivers to a device that gave a push target. The outer members are Apple's and Google's own; ours are the alert's words and the three members that say which notice it is and the page the app opens. A push carries no link, no token and no address.
encoding: compact JSON, members in the order below, strings escaped as coax/lib/json writes them (UTF-8 as it is)

apns.name: aps.alert.body
apns.rule: the notice's words (auth.notices.words), at most 400 characters

apns.name: oa.what
apns.rule: the notice's kind, as auth.notices.what: recovery.start, link.nostr, wallet.limit.raise and the rest

apns.name: oa.open
apns.rule: "/settings/security": the page the app opens when the notice is tapped. An app opens nothing else from a push

fcm.name: message.data.notice
fcm.rule: oa.notice as decimal digits (Google's data values are strings)

goldens.name: apns-recovery-start

values.title: OpenAgents security: someone asked to recover your account
values.body: Someone logged in to your OpenAgents account with its email and asked to recover it. If nothing stops it, after 2026-11-15 14:02 UTC a new key they choose replaces every key and passkey on the account. Logging in with your key or passkey cancels it, and you can cancel it from this notice.
